To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the excitatory monosynthatic and inhibitory synaptic transmission in spino neurons are suppressed and the excitatory polysynthatic transmission is facilitated after cerebral ischemia in rat.

the excitatory monosynthesis, the inhibitory synaptic component and the excitability of spino neurons were suppressed after ischemic insult whereas the excitatory polsynaptic component was facilitated.

the inhibitory synaptic input to spiny neurons is abolished after ischemia whereas the facilitation of polysynaptic excitatory transmission in neostiratum is stronger in the ipsilateral neostriatum compared with the contralateral one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential changes of synaptic transmission and intrinsic membrane properties in spiny neurons in left and right hemi-neostriatum after cerebral ischemia.
the changes of synaptic transmission and membrane properties of striatal spiny neurons in vivo.
the changes of synaptic transmission and the intrinsic membrane properties in spiny neurons after ischemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the excitatory synaptic transmission is facilitated whereas the inhibitory synaptic and the intrinsic excitability of neurons in neostiratium are suppressed after transient forebrain ischemia.
the excitatory synaptic transmission is depressed and the inhibitory synaptic activity and excitability of neostriatal neurons are reduced following transient forebrain ischaemia.
the inhibitory synaptic input is more vulnerable than excitatory input in spiny neurons following ischemia and this vulnerability is stronger in the left neocortex than in the right neocortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the excitatory monosynthesis and the intrinsic excitability are suppressed, the excitatory polysynthesis and the inhibitory monosynthesis are facilitated, and the inhibitory polysynthesis is completely abolished after ischemic insult.

the ischemia-induced suppression of excitatory and inhibitory synaptic transmission in neostrial spiny neurons may result from the impairment of glutamatergic and GABAergic presynaptic mechanisms and that the facilitation of late depolarizing polysynaptic potentials may result from the enhancement of glutamateric postsynaptic mechanisms.
the inhibitory synaptic input is more important for maintaining the excitability of spines in neostriatal medium-sized spiny neurons than excitatory input.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the excitatory polysnaptic pathway in the striatum is facilitated after transient forebrain ischaemia and that the facilitation of the excitatory polysnyptic pathway in the right neosrtiatum is stronger than that in the left neosrtiatium.
the excitatory polysinaptic transmission in neosstriatum was potentiated after ischemia and the inhibitory component was depressed.
the excitatory polysnaptic transmission was facilitated after ischemia.
